Single-phase AC path

Current, voltage, and power factor feeding a real watt result

Formula Watts = Amps x 220V x PF

Quick answer

Use this calculator to convert AC current into real watts with voltage and power factor.

Single-phase AC loads can be resistive or inductive. Resistive loads may be near PF 1.00, while motors, compressors, and HVAC equipment often need a lower power factor.

Watts = Amps x 220V x PF

Inputs to check before calculating

  • Use the correct nominal voltage for the circuit.
  • Enter measured current or nameplate running current.
  • Use realistic PF for motors, compressors, and transformer loads.
  • Compare the result with breaker and continuous-load limits.

Example: 10 amps at 220 volts

At 220 volts, 10 amps equals 2,200 watts before AC power-factor adjustments. Formula: 10 A x 220 V = 2,200 W.

Best use cases

  • Appliance load planning
  • AC power factor option
  • kW conversion included
  • single-phase AC load planning with clear unit labels.

Common mistake to avoid

Do not use DC-style amps x volts for every AC load when the equipment has a lower power factor.

How to use the result

Use the watt result for appliance planning, branch-circuit checks, and comparison with the main amps to watts formula.

Accuracy and safety note

Calculator output is a planning estimate. Final breaker sizing, wire gauge, derating, voltage-drop limits, equipment protection, and code compliance should be verified with manufacturer documentation and a qualified electrician or engineer.

FAQ

220V Calculator FAQ

Fast answers before you use the calculator or compare formulas.

W How do I convert amps to watts at 220V?

Multiply amps by 220 volts. For resistive loads: Watts = Amps × 220. For AC motors and compressors: Watts = Amps × 220 × Power Factor. Example: 10 amps at 220V = 2,200 watts.

VS Is 220V the same as 230V or 240V?

220V, 230V, and 240V are different nominal voltages used in different regions. 220V is common in parts of Asia, Africa, and South America. 230V is the EU/UK standard (harmonized from 220V). 240V is US split-phase. The actual measured voltage can vary by ±10%, so a "220V" outlet may read 215V–225V.

APP What appliances run on 220V?

In countries with 220V mains, virtually all household appliances run on 220V: air conditioners, washing machines, water heaters, ovens, irons, and refrigerators. In the US, 220V is less common but used for heavy appliances imported from international markets.

15A How many watts can a 220V, 15A circuit deliver?

A 220V, 15A circuit can deliver 3,300 watts maximum (15 × 220). At 80% continuous load, the planning limit is 2,640 watts. This is significantly more than a 120V, 15A circuit (1,800W), which is why 220V systems can handle larger appliances on lighter circuits.

CAL Do I need a different calculator for 220V vs 120V?

The formula is identical — only the voltage value changes. However, the dedicated 220V calculator presets the voltage to 220, saving time and reducing input errors. It also includes 220V-specific guidance for international wiring standards and appliance ratings.

⚠ Can I plug a 120V appliance into 220V?

No — plugging a 120V-rated appliance directly into 220V can destroy it and create a fire hazard. The appliance would draw roughly double its rated current, overheating internal components. Use a step-down transformer or a dual-voltage appliance (look for "100–240V" on the nameplate).
